parsed.explanation: Combined regime, rated as one system. Documented traveller-facing exposures compound: a national passport marker regime that has blocked or confiscated documents and left travellers stranded; an entry cable that refuses mismatched applicants and can trigger a lifetime fraud ineligibility finding; a state law imposing birth-sex facility rules in public buildings (including airports) with penalties and private bounty suits; licence invalidation for trans holders; and national custody harms (forced labour, sexual abuse, reported denial of care). Protections are partial: a national hate-crimes statute, national employment law, and some injunctions. None is documented as operating for visitors against these exposures. No trans-specific killing rate is documented. Multiple exposures are universal and enforced by the state, so the score sits in the high-risk band.

entry_documents.exposure: National passports issue only M or F by supporting documents; existing X passports expire; markers not matching birth sex are refused. Passports confiscated or blocked, leaving travellers stranded. Entry cable refuses discrepant applicants and may trigger a lifetime fraud ineligibility finding (never automatic, waivers limited). Ally governments have issued advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiry. A civil-liberties suit is pending; the Supreme Court has allowed the restrictions to take effect. Not documented as operating for visitors.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch at entry leads to refusal, questioning, and possible permanent ineligibility. The same mismatch then carries into state-level ID checks and facility rules during any internal travel.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: One documented arrest for trans restroom use (handcuffed, charged with trespass, held 24 hours in men's ward). Immigration custody: reported forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans men. National corrections policy adopted from 2026 imposes hair cutting, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution; the bureau stopped reporting trans prisoner numbers.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Pretrial release was granted in the arrest case. Trespass requires refusal to leave after a request, not automatic arrest. Not documented as operating beyond that.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A facility-rule arrest can place a visitor in a birth-sex ward. Document discrepancy at entry can lead to investigation and custody, so custody harms are reachable from routine border or facility encounters.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Nine states plus one unit ban gender-identity facility use in all government buildings. Nine more cover schools and some government buildings; three cover schools only. Six extend to some private settings. Four criminalise certain bathroom use. The state law covers publicly owned buildings including airports, with fines up to $1,000 and bounty suits of at least $1,000 by any private person. Licence invalidation applies to existing credentials.
federal_state_facilities.protection: About 29 states, four units and the capital district have no such ban in mapped categories. The map notes other sex-definition rules may still apply. The state's 2020 anti-discrimination law covers employment, housing and public accommodations for businesses with four or more employees.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Universal facility exposure applies to any visitor using a public building. Private bounty enforcement does not need a prosecutor, so the exposure reaches private actors as well as the state. Invalidated licences create a document mismatch at airports and hotels.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care for minors under 18 is banned in the state and in 27 states overall. Proposed national rules would bar public insurance reimbursement for under-18 care. National funding cut-offs and youth-service closures on the crisis lifeline. Hospitals subpoenaed for under-19 records including names and SSNs.
care_services.protection: Court injunctions have blocked some orders. Not documented as protecting visitors' adult care access.
care_services.interaction: Records subpoenas and care bans can disclose a traveller or minor's history to state authorities. Care denial becomes more likely if a visitor needs treatment during a trip.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism strategy (May 2026) names 'radically pro-transgender' groups for priority neutralisation. A December 2025 memorandum uses 'radical gender ideology' among extremist indicators and sets up a reward system. An executive order directs law enforcement to prosecute teachers who facilitate a trans minor's social transition. Government statements frame trans status as a state threat.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The strategy states powers will not target people who simply disagree. Several orders are enjoined. Not documented as protecting trans travellers.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing at national level shapes how officers and courts treat trans people in entry, custody and facility enforcement. It raises discovery and escalation risk for visitors.

minors_guardians.exposure: Travelling with a minor: K-12 facility bans in 21 states, with school-based enforcement. The state bans under-18 care. Teachers face prosecution threats for preferred names. School sports are restricted. Passport and document rules apply to minors through their parent's documents. A parent may face guardian inquiry if a child's care or school status is challenged.
minors_guardians.protection: Injunctions have blocked some school-related orders. Parental lawsuit injunction in May 2026. Not documented as protecting travelling families.
minors_guardians.interaction: A facility or document incident involving a child exposes the accompanying adult to the same penalties and custody rules. Care or school rules can separate or expose the family.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence rate or street-violence record documented. The bounty mechanism creates private-actor exposure: any person can sue a trans traveller encountered in a wrong-sex facility. Lawsuits filed by two trans men cite fear of violence. Bias statistics are for sexual orientation, not gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.protection: A national hate-crimes statute covers gender identity. Only 23 states cover gender identity in bias-violence statutes. The state's hate-crime law does not cover gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Private bounty suits can turn a facility encounter into a civil claim or confrontation. Police response to trans victims is not documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Lawsuits against the passport policy and the state facility and ID law are unresolved. Number of invalidation notices and bounty suits is not recorded. Enforcement data for the facility and ID provisions is not sourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Court injunctions have blocked several national orders. The national hate-crimes statute and state anti-discrimination law operate in some states. Remedies have not been shown to work for visitors against passport, facility or custody exposures.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Pending litigation means the rules in force at the time of travel are uncertain. Reliance on court relief does not reduce exposure on any given trip.

anchor_checks.comparison: Closest analogue: birth-sex housing and cross-dressing arrests in administrative buildings, with brief sentences and no execution. This dossier adds private bounty suits, national passport refusal, ID invalidation and documented immigration-custody sexual abuse, so it sits at or below 0.25-C on the custody and enforcement axes. It is higher than 0.25-C because no capital or extortion-based custody practice is documented.

Entry exclusion by register with no arrest and no effective appeal. This dossier has similar entry refusal and fraud-ground exposure and a similar lack of effective appeal. It is lower than 0.35-A because it adds facility-based arrests, licence invalidation, custody harms and bounty suits that reach a visitor without state initiation.

Secondary screening with discretionary denial, administrative consequences only and a remote chance of criminal exposure. This dossier has comparable screening but adds documented arrests, custody sexual abuse and birth-sex facility penalties, so it sits below 0.55-B.

Permissive border practice, respectful inspection and brief detention with compensation. This dossier lacks all three: a documented fraud-based exclusion route, documented custody harm and state threat framing. Reaching 0.75 would require documented acceptance of foreign documents, facilities congruent with identity, and working remedies against bounty suits.

Full acceptance with independent oversight and no detention exposure. This dossier is far below: birth-sex facility rules in public buildings, document invalidation and documented custody abuse are all operative. Reaching 0.95 would require removal of the bounty, facility and document exposures and documented custody protection.

parsed.synthesis: The national passport refusal, the entry fraud ground, the state facility-and-ID regime and the custody harms interact along the journey. A discrepant document can trigger entry refusal, investigation, and custody or facility exposure. The state bounty law adds private enforcement that reaches any visitor using a public building, including an airport. National threat framing and the care and school rules extend exposure to travelling minors and guardians. Documented protections (a national hate-crimes statute, state anti-discrimination law in some states, same-sex marriage, and some enjoined orders) do not operate against these visitor-facing exposures. Violence is not documented at a trans-specific level. The combined score reflects tier-1 state-imposed universal exposure with no working remedy, placing the jurisdiction in the high-risk band.
